results.title: Trial Emulation Methods
results.content: Target trial emulation is one approach to estimating treatment effects with observation data. There are 7 key components of a target trial protocol: eligibility criteria, treatment strategies, treatment assignment, follow-up period, outcomes, causal con-trasts, and statistical analysis plan. In our example of the target trial of rosuvastatin, treatment-naı ¨ve patients without a history of hematuria, protein-uria, or end-stage kidney disease (ie, study outcomes) at the time of randomization (ie, time zero) between 2011 and 2019 would be eligible (Table 1). Time zero in an RCT is when an eligible individual initiates a treatment strategy and the outcomes begin to be counted (ie, time of randomization). • Future information after time zero must not be used to determine eligibility in target trial emulation to avoid selection bias Treatment strategies (1) Initiation of rosuvastatin (treatment of interest) (2) Initiation of atorvastatin (comparison strategy) When clinically warranted during the follow-up, patients and providers decide whether to stop or switch therapy. • Use of active comparator (eg, rosuvastatin vs atorvastatin) is helpful to minimize confounding bias Treatment assignment Individuals are randomly assigned to a strategy at baseline and will be aware of their assigned treatment group (no masking). • Selecting time zero correctly in observational analyses is critical to avoid bias (eg, immortal time bias and selection bias) Outcome Hematuria and proteinuria ascertained by laboratory measurements • Differential outcome ascertainment by treat-ment strategy is a source of bias when pro-vider ’s knowledge of treatment status (no masking) affects provider ’s decision to monitor the outcomes Causal contrasts / statistical analyses Intention-to-treat effect, ignoring adherence to the treatment strategies Survival analysis for time-to event outcome. In observational studies, intention-to-treat effects can be estimated using treatment assignment at time zero. As described above, common sources of bias in target trial emulation include confounding bias, selection bias, differential outcome ascertainment, and immortal time bias. 6 Importantly, propensity score methods (which are designed to address confounding bias) require the assumption that there are no unmeasured differences between treatment groups, conditional on the observed covariates. Quantification of treatment effects using well-conducted observational studies, especially those following the target trial emulation framework, can complement and expand the evidence from RCTs. results.title: Current practices in studies applying the target trial emulation framework: a protocol for a systematic review | BMJ Open
results.content: * Current practices in studies applying the target trial emulation framework: a protocol for a systematic review. Current practices in studies applying the target trial emulation framework: a protocol for a systematic review. The aim of this systematic review is to investigate the practices of studies applying the target trial emulation framework to evaluate the effectiveness of interventions. Target trial emulation is a framework for the application of RCT design principles to emulate a hypothetical open-label RCT (the hypothetical target trial) using existing observational data as the primary data source as opposed to the prospective recruitment and measurement of randomised units.4 Because treatment assignment is neither blind nor random, valid causal treatment effects are estimated if the identification principles of causal inference are satisfied.4–8 These include the assumptions of exchangeability (participants in a study may be swapped between treatment and control groups without changing the average treatment effect), consistency (no multiple versions of the treatment options being investigated), positivity (every patient has a non-zero probability to receive every treatment option under investigation given their measured covariates) and non-interference (the treatment given to one patient does not affect the outcome of another patient).7 9–13 A table of acronyms, abbreviations and technical terms are defined in online supplemental appendix. Target trial emulation studies can be credible sources of real-world evidence (RWE) to support regulatory decisions in the absence of RCTs, for instance, within the Food and Drug Administration’s Real-World Evidence Program16 and the European Medicines Agency’s OPerational, TechnIcal, and MethodologicAL framework (OPTIMAL).17 Furthermore, with the increasing availability of large-scale real-world data (RWD) especially those seen in research cohorts, registry, hospital and general practitioner databases, there is impetus for increased popularity of the application of target trial emulation. First, a systematic review (SR) that reports on the design, conduct and reporting of target trial emulation studies will help facilitate new research hoping to use the methodology. 1. To review how trial emulation studies have designed their target trial specification (eligibility criteria, treatment strategies, treatment assignment, outcomes, time zero and follow-up, causal contrasts, statistical analysis). Additional inclusion criteria are as follows: (1) meets study definition of target trial emulation study; (2) peer-reviewed reports, protocols (published or archived), study registrations and conference presentations on original research studies that used/plan to use the trial emulation, from all fields of research; and (3) available in English language.

results.title: Target Trial Emulation Framework - Lumanity
results.content: # Target Trial Emulation Framework. Target trial emulation (TTE)-oriented study designs can improve real world evidence (RWE) acceptability, mitigate bias, evaluate clinically relevant treatment strategy, and overcome temporal challenges. Observational studies in pharmacoepidemiology play a pivotal role in clinical decision-making when randomized controlled trials (RCT) are practically or ethically infeasible to conduct. The TTE framework is a structured approach that can be applied to observational studies to emulates the conditions and protocol of an ideal hypothetical RCT, addressing sources of bias. This approach is recommended by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, European Medicines Agency, National Institute for Health and Care Excellence in the UK for observational studies with causal objectives to minimize the risk of bias. > “TTE is not just a technical tool, but a bridge to enhance the transparency and structure of RWE studies”. > – Jetty Overbeek, Head of Research, PHARMO, part of Lumanity. Application of the TTE Framework. 1. Select fit-for-purpose data: The right dataset can effectively support robust causal inference. Clinical richness is essential for capturing key covariates, such as patient demographics, comorbidities, and biomarkers, enabling accurate comparisons between treatment groups. Longitudinal depth tracks the conditions of each treatment strategy over time and accounts for time-varying confounders that influence outcomes. Data quality and completeness can minimize information bias and residual confounding. 2. Specify the target trial protocol and emulate it with real world data (RWD): The protocol should define the causal question of interest, eligibility criteria, treatment strategies, treatment assignment procedures, outcomes, follow-up, causal contrasts, and statistical analysis.
